master.one_liner: Voronoi whose cell size follows a source node continuously across any size range, with no shear or seams, for the price of two cellular searches.
master.look: Cells grade smoothly from huge to tiny, with fine cells budding along the boundary of large ones. Reads like graded sediment, cracked mud that tightens near a river, or foam. Good for biome-driven rock size, paving, skin scales and masks.
master.algorithm: Inputs: hybrid Level l(p) in [0, Levels-1). L=floor(l). For j in {0,1}: fr=Base*Ratio^(L+j) (per lane); search the 3^D window at p*fr with seed+(L+j)*prime, giving F1_j, F2_j in that level's own lattice units and hash h_j. Penalty pen_j=k*|L+j-l|. Candidates are F1_j+pen_j and F2_j+pen_j. b1 and b2 are the smallest and second smallest candidates, id is the hash of b1. Output: CellValue=rnd(id), Crack=sat((b2-b1)*gain), Pillow=rnd(id)*smoothstep(0,w,b2-b1). Why two searches are enough: when l crosses an integer the search set changes from {L,L+1} to {L+1,L+2}. At that moment the outgoing and incoming levels both carry penalty k, so k above the largest F2 (about 1.6) means neither can win. Proto mode 7 searches all levels and mode 13 searches two. Both give c0ratio 8.00 at k about 1.5-1.6 and look the same.
master.why_new: Today, a per-pixel scale on a lattice shears, and Size Jitter is limited by the window. Fade across fixed scales needs one Cellular per scale and cross-dissolves the patterns instead of making real cell boundaries. Here the boundaries are real across scales and the cost does not depend on the level range.
master.simd_plan: No lane branching. The lattice frequency is just a per-lane float, so lanes can sit on different levels. Each search is a normal CellularDistance F1/F2 pass; the merge is Min/Select on floats and ids. Cost is 2x CellularDistance plus one Level eval: about 8 / 24 / 82 ns for 2D/3D/4D, or about 7x Perlin in 2D. Dimension agnostic.
master.continuity: C0 (c0ratio 8.00 with the 5x5 proto window) for Crack and Pillow, because b1 and b2 are order statistics of continuous values. CellValue is deliberately discontinuous at cell borders only.
master.params: Level (hybrid), Levels range, Base Scale, Ratio (default 2), Blend k (lower lets levels mix but then needs more searches), Jitter, Output enum, Distance function.
master.risks: The proto used a 5x5 window, so 3x3 F2 errors at jitter 1 may show as small jumps at level changes; test at Jitter 0.8-1. Below the k limit, seams appear on integer crossings of Level. A steep Level gradient compresses the transition band.

master.one_liner: Foam field from how evenly a point is shared between nearby sites: smooth, no sorting, with Plateau-border thickening at junctions and curved pressure walls.
master.look: Prototyped. 2D: bubble raft, thin soft bright walls that flare at triple junctions, small round bubbles sitting on large ones (press 0.5 to 0.9). 3D slice: round bubble cross-sections with soft membranes. 3D isosurface: g<0.2 gives pebble-like polygonal bubble cells with narrow gaps; g>0.2 gives open-cell foam or metal-foam struts. Use for foam, sea foam, bone, soap films, cell tissue, cloud cell masks. w animates sites and pressures.
master.algorithm: Lattice: jittered sites as CellularDistance, window 3^dim. For each site i: d2 = |p-s_i|^2; r_i = 1 + Pressure*rnd11(hash bits), rr = r_i^2; a_i = max(rr/(d2+1e-3) - rr/Rc^2, 0) (Franke-Little form, compact at Rc); w_i = a_i^k with integer k by repeated squaring (k=4). Rc must not exceed the distance to the nearest site outside the window: Rc = 1.1 for jitter radius 0.4 (GridJitter 0.8). S1 = sum w_i, S2 = sum w_i^2. g = (S1^2 - S2)/(S1^2 + eps). g is 0 inside a cell, 1/2 on a two-cell wall, 2/3 on a three-cell edge, 3/4 at a four-cell vertex, because it is the Gini-Simpson participation index of the Shepard membership p_i = w_i/S1. Output ScaleOutput(g, 0, 0.75). Pressure gives multiplicative weights, so walls become spherical Apollonius caps and small bubbles bulge into large ones, as Young-Laplace predicts. A threshold on g gives a wall thickness that grows at junctions by itself.
master.why_new: F2-F1 has creases, flat walls and no junction thickening, and needs sorting. A soft wall needs F1..F4 together, which CellularDistance cannot combine. The Gini field has 3 and 4 cell information with no sort, so it is a single smooth value with no crease inside walls. Clearly unlike the CellularDistance tiles on the contact sheet.

cell-frame.look: Random mode with aniso 6: fibre bundles, each Voronoi grain a patch of parallel streaks at its own angle, like felted or brushed fibres / metal grains; the grain boundaries are soft and the streak direction changes cleanly between patches. Guided mode: the streaks follow the contours of the guide field across grains, a wind-streak / wood-grain / fur look with the patches still faintly visible. The gentle-source test shows the difference the barycentric blend makes: the two-sample blend has fan-shaped facets around every triple junction, the barycentric blend gives smooth ridges along the walls and clean junctions. 3D form exists (3x3x3, Householder frames, Perlin fbm source, 4-grain blend) and the XZ slice shows the same streaked grains.

cell-frame.artifacts: Two-sample blend: t=(d2-d1)/((d2-d0)+(d2-d1)) is undefined at triple junctions, fan facets everywhere (gentle probe: 564 probe pairs with |diff|>0.02 at h=1e-3, c0ratio 2.8, max slope 457). Same probe: 22 pairs > 0.02, all at near-4-fold points (d3 - d0 ~0.004, weight sum ~0.005): steep continuous ramps over sub-pixel regions, no facets on the sheet. c0ratio 6.5 with the busy source, 1.76 on the gentle probe because the metric is a max over those spots. Cap needs d0 < cap, so Jitter <= 0.9 in 2D, 0.7 in 3D. Blend width is now a true width, 0.25-0.5 looks right.
cell-frame.node_shape: Meta node CellFrame: Source (generator), Guide (optional generator), Cell Scale, Aniso, Scale Jitter, Angle Jitter, Blend Width, Grid Jitter (<=0.9 / 0.7). Cap = 1.5 - 0.437*Jitter - eps; clamp Jitter in the setter. Guided needs the gradient of another generator at the feature point.

master.one_liner: Runs any source graph in a different frame per Voronoi grain (rotation, stretch, scale, seed) with a seam-free two-sample blend; a guide source turns the grains into flow-aligned texture without integration.
master.look: Random mode: fibre bundles, woven patches, metal grains, feathers, brushed-metal tiles. Guided mode: fur, wind streaks, wood grain and hair flowing around the contours of another noise, a line integral convolution look at a fixed cost.
master.algorithm: Search window for F1,F2,F3 (d0<=d1<=d2) and hashes/seed positions. Blend: t=(d2-d1)/((d2-d0)+(d2-d1)+eps), which is exactly 0.5 when d0=d1 and exactly 0 when d1=d2, so the second sample fades out before its identity can change. w=0.5*sat((t-(0.5-Width))/Width). Frame per grain from hash: unit axis n, scale f; q=(p+(Aniso-1)*n*dot(n,p))*f. Output=(1-w)*Source(seed^h0,q0)+w*Source(seed^h1,q1). Guided mode: n=normalized gradient of Guide by finite difference at the grain's seed position, optionally with a small angle jitter from hash; high frequency across the gradient makes streaks run along Guide's contours. Frame comes from one point per grain and is constant within it, so nothing shears, however wild the guide.
master.why_new: CellularLookup samples at the cell centre but cannot transform a graph's domain per cell. A per-pixel rotation or stretch shears far from the origin; picking the frame per grain avoids that entirely. It gives Source graphs orientation fields, which FastNoise has no way to express now.
master.simd_plan: One window pass extended to F3 (about 15% over CellularDistance), then 2 Source evals with per-lane position and seed. The axis stretch is dimension agnostic. With Source=FBm 3 octaves: about 11 / 30 / 75 ns in 2D/3D/4D. Guided adds 2*(D+1) guide evals, so a cheap guide is required, about +15 ns in 2D with a 2-octave guide.
master.continuity: C0 everywhere except for a bounded singular point at exact triple junctions where the weight is undefined, invisible on the sheets. Measured c0ratio 2.0-2.3, but the sources are highly stretched and steep, so that metric does not separate seam from slope here; run a dedicated seam test before trusting it. No visible seams on the sheets.
master.params: Source (generator), Guide (optional generator), Cell Scale, Aniso, Scale Jitter, Angle Jitter, Blend Width, Grid Jitter.
master.risks: The proto used a 5x5 window; at 3x3 an incorrect F3 at full jitter could cause small jumps, so limit Jitter to about 0.7. Guided mode has sign flips of n harmlessly, since stretch is even in n. At guide critical points the gradient is near 0 and direction is arbitrary. Cross-fades lose contrast slightly in borders.
master.cost_note: Guided adds 2*(D+1) guide evals, so a cheap guide is required, about +15 ns in 2D with a 2-octave guide.

nested-voronoi.look: Terrazzo / conglomerate: large unbroken polished stones (gap) sitting in fields of progressively finer rubble, every child cell clipped exactly by its parent wall, each parent's children at their own density and orientation. Crack output (out=2) shows the big stones as bright slabs among dark fine mortar; depth output (out=3) maps which cells stayed whole. gap=0 is a plain 3-level polycrystal, gap=0.6 mostly whole stones with a few shattered ones; aniso=3 turns the children into oriented fibre bundles per parent (bark / metal grain). 3D vol (out=2, iso -0.6) is a packing of large polyhedral stones among fine rubble.
nested-voronoi.dims: 2D and 3D measured (real 3x3x3 per level with 3D Householder reflection and stretch; slice and vol rendered). 4D is 3 levels x 81 points, expensive.
nested-voronoi.range: [-1,1]: check over 8 seeds min -0.999 max 1.000, far coords fine, no NaN
nested-voronoi.artifacts: c0ratio 8.00 for the crack output at jit 1 (7.99 with aniso 3) in 3x3: the parent F2-F1 term reaches 0 on the parent wall so the child lattice can change freely there. Children only approximately clipped where the 3x3 F2 is inexact (rare at jit 1, as in CellularDistance). Scalar early-out per lane becomes a mask in a port, so cost is always Levels passes. Fine levels alias at high lacunarity.
nested-voronoi.node_shape: Own node NestedVoronoi (Levels, Lacunarity, Gap, Frequency Jitter, Aniso, Age, Crack Width, Output enum) or a mode on a hierarchical cellular node; natural complement to GradedVoronoi (same kernel, size grading by parent instead of by a Level source).
nested-voronoi.port_notes: Loop over Levels (int member): seed for level L is the previous winner's hash (int32v per lane), frequency and frame from hash bits (fr = lac^L*(1+fj*rnd), Householder reflection q -= 2n(n.q), stretch along m), standard F1/F2 window pass, crack = Min(crack, age*L + 0.5*(F2-F1)/fr), id = Select(alive, h1, id). Alive mask ANDed down the levels. Dimension agnostic. Shares the window kernel with GradedVoronoi.

master.one_liner: Each Voronoi cell owns a private child Voronoi with its own seed, density, orientation and stretch, and may stay unbroken, giving terrazzo and polycrystal looks.
master.look:
Large polished stones sitting in fields of rubble, terrazzo, conglomerate rock, or metal grains with differently oriented sub-cells. The Gap parameter is what makes the size distribution so bimodal.
[HierarchicalCracks, nature-phenomena] Mud-crack mosaics where newer cracks end against older, wider ones. Tilt gives curled, shard-like plates, anisotropy gives furrowed bark, and one level with rounding gives striking giraffe or pebble patches.
master.algorithm:
id=0 start: level 0 search gives F1,F2,h. crack=0.5*(F2-F1), id=h. For L=1..Levels-1: h'=mix(id,L). alive=rnd(h'>>a)>=Gap; once a lane dies it stays frozen. fr=Lac^L*(1+FreqJitter*rnd(h'>>b)). q=p reflected through the Householder plane from hash n (q-=2n(n.q)), then stretched along hash axis m (q+=(Aniso-1)m(m.q)), times fr. Search q with seed=h'. crack=min(crack, Age*L+0.5*(F2-F1)/fr); id=hash of the child's F1. Output: rnd(id)*smoothstep(0,w,crack), rnd(id), or crack. The key trick is that a child lattice seeded from the parent's id can differ arbitrarily across a parent border, because the crack term reaches 0 exactly there.

[HierarchicalCracks, nature-phenomena] pid=0. For each level l: seed_l=seed+1000*l+pid (a per-lane int32v). Pass 1: search the 3^D window for the nearest point, keeping its vector vn and hash. Pass 2: over the same stored points, e=min((0.5*(vi+vn)).(vi-vn)/|vi-vn|), skipping the nearest point itself; this is the exact bisector distance. Convert to world units e/f_l; out=min(out, saturate(e/(f_l*width_l)))) with e already in world units after that conversion; pid=pid*31+nearest hash. Options: Corner Rounding replaces min in pass 2 with smin(k), giving rounded plates (giraffe, cobbles). Anisotropy scales one axis before the distance. Plate Tilt adds (cos a, sin a).vn/f on the last level with angle a from the hash. Output is sqrt(out)*(1+plate).
master.why_new: Voronoi fracturing is usually done with two independent layers, where children cross parent borders. Here children are clipped by parents, and density, orientation and survival change per parent, which no graph of existing nodes can do (no node passes a cell id to a child's seed or domain).
master.simd_plan: Seed is already int32v per lane in Gen, so per-lane re-seeding fits directly. Positions from pass 1 go in a fixed stack array of float32v. Estimates per level: 8 ns in 2D, 24 ns in 3D, 75 ns in 4D, so 3 levels are about 24 ns in 2D (6x CellularDistance-level cost per 3 levels) and 72 ns in 3D. An F2-F1 mode costs one CellularDistance per level (4/12/41 ns). 4D is expensive.
master.continuity: C0 for crack and for rnd(id)*fade, measured at c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 6. Use F2-F1, not the exact bisector formula (see notes). Raw id output jumps by design.
master.params: Levels (int), Lacunarity, Gap (hybrid at parent is not possible at pixel level; use hash, or sample a source at the parent seed), Frequency Jitter, Aniso, Age, Crack Width, Output enum.
master.risks:
Age must rise with level or C0 breaks. Fine levels alias if Lacunarity is high. 4D cost is heavy; offer 2 levels for tileable use. The 3D form was not rendered; proto Eval3 is only a sheared 2D slice.
[HierarchicalCracks, nature-phenomena] Real cracks meet at near 90 degrees; here child cracks meet parents at arbitrary angles. Pass 2 in a 3^D window is an approximation: the reference two-pass code uses 5x5, while the Blender change reduced it to 3x3. Hybrid per-level seed cost is linear in levels but 4D is heavy.
master.cost_note: Estimates per level: 8 ns in 2D, 24 ns in 3D, 75 ns in 4D, so 3 levels are about 24 ns in 2D (6x CellularDistance-level cost per 3 levels) and 72 ns in 3D.
master.variant_notes: Child lattice reseeded per lane by the parent's hash. HierarchicalCracks adds exact bisector option, plate tilt and corner rounding. Crack age must rise with level for C0.

cellular-planes.look: Hard mode (S=0): a Voronoi tiling where every cell is a tilted plane, each tile shows its own gradient direction and ends at a step; hillshade reads as faulted blocks. Relief at 14 cells across (S=0.05, hscale 50) reads as tumbled slate / tilted plates with cliffs between them, clearly unlike CellularValue's flat steps. S=0.1-0.3 softens the steps into ramps between tilted plateaus (soft fault lines); S>=0.6 is a mushy smooth-Voronoi hill field that looks like generic noise, so the sharp end is the value. 3D vol (S=0.05, iso 0) gives polyhedral shards with planar cut faces. src=1 (Perlin lift at the feature point) gives plates whose heights follow a large-scale uplift map at lower contrast.
cellular-planes.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3x3x3 with 3D tilt vectors; slice and vol rendered). 4D is a direct GenT extension, not built.
cellular-planes.range: Normalised by 1/(lift+0.75*tilt) then clamped: measured min -0.998 max 1.000 over 8 seeds (clamp rarely hit), std ~0.30, no NaN
cellular-planes.artifacts: c0ratio 7.92 (S=0.1), 7.98 (0.3), 8.0 (0.6, 1.0), 1.0 at S=0 by design. Window theory: an out-of-window cell can have (d_out - d1) near 0 at the worst corner, so above S~0.3 a weight can pop at window edges in rare spots; none visible in the S=0.3 or 0.6 sheets and the FFT axis value (~20) equals hard mode's, so it is the sharp-edged field, not lattice lines. Dark bands in hillshade at S=0.3-0.6 are wall ramps. Cap Smoothness at ~0.4 in the setter.
cellular-planes.node_shape: CellularPlanes node: Jitter, Lift (hybrid), Tilt (hybrid), Tilt Bias, Smoothness 0..0.4, Flatten, optional Lift Source (sampled at the feature point), Feature Scale, Seed, Output Min/Max.
cellular-planes.port_notes: Pass 1 F1 (exact with 0.437 disc jitter); pass 2 over the same 3^D points: weight = Max(0, 1 - (d - d1)*invS) raised by m squarings, plane = lift*rnd11(h) - tiltMag*Dot(tiltDir, featureVec); accumulate sum w and sum w*plane, one Reciprocal. Hard mode is a Select on the F1 index. Squared distances (lin=0) also give 7.97 and save the sqrt. Lift and Tilt are hybrids.

critic.notes: Honest terrain use, but hard mode is not a new capability. A graph of 5 CellularLookup nodes (lift plus two tilt terms from Gradient minus Gradient at the feature point) gives the same tilted slabs at 20.75 / 68.38 / 256.22 ns AVX2, so unique stays low. Reasons to keep it: cost (estimate about 5-8 ns against 21 ns measured; FBm of the stock graph measured 79.56 / 275.61 / 1048.99 ns on its White form) and the soft S range, which no graph reaches. It belongs on CellularValue as Tilt and Smoothness, with 0 keeping today's output. Jump numbers: bisection on every pixel edge, threshold 0.03, 6 seeds, 1536 unit^2 unless noted. 0 means none found above threshold in that area, not a proof. Challenge: the Smoothness 0.4 cap is not enough at jitter 1, and c0ratio 7.92-8.0 cannot see it. Jitter 1: S 0.06 0, S 0.1 0.0001 max 0.044, S 0.15 0.0003 max 0.071, S 0.3 0.0013 max 0.105, S 0.4 0.0031 max 0.132, and S 0.6 c0ratio 0.93-1.18 with a straddling probe. Jitter 0.8: 0 up to S 0.4. master.one_liner: Worley cells carrying a random plane (height + tilt) instead of a flat value: faulted blocks, tilted plates, crystal facets; a Smoothness parameter blends the planes with smooth-Voronoi weights into a continuous fault-block terrain.
master.look:
Horst-and-graben terrain, tilted slate blocks, tumbled basalt, shingled plains: each block has a clear dip direction and ends at a cliff. Hillshade reads as geological faulting. Clearly unlike CellularValue, whose cells are flat, or any smooth noise. Prototyped: rel_fault p=2 and p=4 are the good range.
[CellularPlanes, terrain-tools-engines] Sharp-edged tilted slabs and stepped fault blocks (basalt columns from above, fractured ice sheets, crystal clusters), and in Smooth mode a continuous landscape of gently tilted plateaus meeting along soft fault lines; in 3D, polyhedral shard volumes. The sheet has flat-per-cell CellularValue only.
master.algorithm:
Pass 1: F1 squared distance d1. Pass 2: for each window cell i: plane_i=v_i+dot(t_i, x-p_i); w_i=max(0, 1-(d_i^2-d1)/S)^m, with m by repeated squaring (constant loop). Output sum(w_i*plane_i)/sum(w_i). The owner always has w=1, so the denominator never vanishes. S->0 gives hard Voronoi tilted tiles; large S gives smooth hills. The proto used simpler absolute weights (1-d^2/R^2)^(2^(p+1)) which underflow at high p and showed gray flats; the F1-relative form fixes that.

[CellularPlanes, terrain-tools-engines] Cellular lattice 3^d with Jitter. Per feature point i: q_i, hashed lift v_i = Lift*rnd11, tilt vector g_i = Tilt*rndDir(h) (unit direction times a hashed magnitude^Bias), plane_i(p) = v_i + g_i . (p - q_i). Hard mode (Smoothness = 0): output plane of the F1 point (track argmin as CellularValue does, but carry q and hash through the Selects). Smooth mode: w_i = exp2(-k*d_i), k = lerp(64, 4, Smoothness); out = sum w_i plane_i / sum w_i (IQ smooth-voronoi weights applied to planes rather than distances). Optional Cell Flatten 0..1 multiplies tilt by (1 - Flatten) near cell centres: facets. Optional Source Lookup: replace v_i with Source(q_i) (like CellularLookup) so plate heights follow a large-scale field (tectonic uplift map). Normalise: |out| <= Lift + Tilt*cellRadius.
master.why_new: Per-cell slope requires the feature point position and a second hashed vector inside the cellular loop; CellularValue/CellularLookup cannot produce gradients within a cell. Gaea Shatter/Plates/Voronoi 'forms' and World Creator Plateaus are the tool-side analogues.
master.simd_plan: 3^D window, plane is one dot, weight one Max plus a fixed count of multiplies, one final Reciprocal. Stack array for d^2 or run F1 first. Estimate 2x CellularDistance, 2D 8 ns, 3D 25 ns, 4D 85 ns. Measured scalar 2.7x worley2 at p=4. Generic GenT.
master.continuity: C0 for S>0 and C-infinity away from the F1 switch: c0ratio 7.87 at p=4 with a max slope near 50. S=0 is discontinuous. Requires (d_out^2-d1) >= S for out-of-window cells: at low sharpness the proto's R=1.3 shows faint grid-line seams in hillshade, so S needs an upper bound.

master.one_liner: Each cell owns a randomly rotated, sized SDF shape (disc, segment/capsule, ellipse, n-gon, square, spokes, star, ring); union/smooth-union/sum them, or run the Voronoi outputs on the shape distances (curved parabolic/hyperbolic walls, elongated cells, Johnson-Mehl growth).
master.look:
Scattered rotated squares, hexagons, sequins, scales, asterisks; with Union + Mask it is a 'shape splatter', with F2-F1 it is a Voronoi whose cells are elongated around capsules and whose walls are parabolic (segment vs point) or hyperbolic (discs of different radii), i.e. visibly curved walls with centres that do not move. Sum gives metaball blobs. Growth mode animates crystal nucleation.
[SegmentCellular, dcc-tools] F1: worm-shaped cells, fingerprint-like pits, wood ray flecks. F2-F1: elongated pebbles with long creases. Line with narrow spread: directional scratches. Line with bend: fibres and hair. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=21. Substance Scratches and Messy Fibers, Modo Scratches and Wires.
[CellularFlake, volumetric-3d4d] Not prototyped. 3D iso, discs with Spread 0.2: thin stacked plates like shale or schist; Spread 1: confetti or shattered ice. Rings: interlocked loops, chain mail or noodle tangle. Segments: hay, felt, needles. 2D slice of discs: short hatched line segments like graphite flakes in cast iron, a look absent from the sheet; 2D form of ring is an outlined circle field.
master.algorithm:
Window loop as Cellular.inl (ring jitter is fine). For each window point: v = S - P_c; hash bits give rotation index (256-entry cos/sin table), size_c = Size*(1 + SizeJitter*rnd11), shape params (segment length L_c, n-gon rotation, spoke count).
  v' = R_c * v / size_c   (2 fmadd for 2D rotation)
  Shape SDF in unit frame, all branch-free:
    Disc: |v'| - 1
    Square: max(|x|,|y|) - 1
    NGon(n <= 8, constant loop): max_k dot(v', u_k) - cos(pi/n), u_k from a table
    Capsule: dist(v', segment(-L,0..L,0)) - 1
    Spokes(k): min_k dist(v', segment(0..u_k*L))
    Star: min(NGon(n), NGon(n) rotated by pi/n with inner apothem)
    Ring: abs(Disc) - Thickness
  d_c = sdf * size_c
Combine (Blend enum):
  Union: F1 = min d_c ; also keep F2 and the owner hash
  SmoothUnion: polynomial smin with K
  Sum: sum_c max(0, 1 - max(d_c,0)/Falloff)^2  (blob density, C1)
Output enum: Distance (= F1 clamped at Dmax), Mask, OwnerValue (rnd11(owner hash), flat per shape), F2-F1 (Voronoi-of-shapes walls), Density.
Growth (Johnson-Mehl) mode: radius_c = Speed*max(0, Time - birth_c) with Time a hybrid (use w or a Constant); unborn shapes get d = +inf via Select: crystals nucleate and grow until they meet.
Consistency: a shape of radius <= Rmax around P_c with |S-P_c|inf >= 1 is at least 1 - Rmax away; clamp Distance at Dmax = 1 - Rmax and the min is exact. For OwnerValue/F2-F1 the usual Cellular caveat applies (nearest in-window shape must be closer than 1 - Rmax: true except at extreme jitter).
3D: rotation from a 256-entry table of random 3x3 rotation matrices (built once), shapes: sphere, box, octahedron (|x|+|y|+|z|-1), capsule, n-prism, 3D spokes.
master.why_new: Cellular nodes only know points with an isotropic metric; Size Jitter already gives circular-arc walls (multiplicative weights), but elongated cells, polygonal/star shapes per cell, capsule-Voronoi (parabolic walls) and per-cell shape ids are not expressible with any graph of existing nodes.
master.simd_plan: Same 3^D loop as Cellular.inl plus per point: table lookup of cos/sin by hash bits (gather or two 256-float constexpr tables indexed via FS::Load per lane; alternatively derive cos/sin from the existing random direction bits already used for jitter: the jitter direction IS a unit vector, reuse it as the rotation), 2D rotation 4 mul, shape 8-40 ops, min/Select chain. 2D: 1.5-3x CellularDistance (6-12 ns). 3D: rotation 9 mul per point x 27 + shape: 1.5-3x Cellular3D (20-35 ns). 4D: skip rotation (use axis-aligned shapes), ~1.3x Cellular4D.
master.continuity: Distance/F2-F1: C0 like Cellular. SmoothUnion: C1. Sum/Density: C1-C2. Mask/OwnerValue: discontinuous.
master.params: Shape enum, Size (hybrid), Size Jitter, Rotation Jitter (0..1), Shape Param (L for capsule/spokes, n for n-gon, thickness for ring), Blend enum {Union, SmoothUnion, Sum}, Smooth K (hybrid), Output enum {Distance, Mask, OwnerValue, F2MinusF1, Density}, Time (hybrid, growth), Grid Jitter (hybrid as in Cellular), Feature Scale.
master.risks:
Large shapes (Rmax near 1) shrink Dmax to nearly 0; keep Size*(1+SizeJitter) <= ~0.6 cells. N-gon SDF without atan2 is an n-term max (fine for n<=8). Many enum combinations: scope the first version to Disc/Square/NGon/Capsule/Spokes.
[CellularShape, shader-community] Exactness of the 3^d window breaks for large primitives (seams/popping where a far primitive would have been nearer); clamp Radius+Jitter/2 <= 0.5 in the setter. N-gon folding costs n reflections. 3D random rotations need a cheap hash-to-rotation (quaternion from 3 uniforms, Shoemake).
[SegmentCellular, dcc-tools] Long Length forces sparse cells or window growth. Directional spread needs a per-dimension direction story: 3D uses member direction plus table cone. Fine lines alias at low sampling.
master.cost_note: 2D: 1.5-3x CellularDistance (6-12 ns). 3D: rotation 9 mul per point x 27 + shape: 1.5-3x Cellular3D (20-35 ns).
master.variant_notes: Worley over SDF primitives. Merged primitives: segment with bend (SegmentCellular: worm cells, scratches), disc and ring (CellularFlake: shale, mica, chain-mail in 3D), and n-gon, box, spokes, star. Also Johnson-Mehl growth via a Time param.

master.one_liner: Fine cells inherit from coarse cells through a deterministic parent chain (nearest coarse point in a 2^D block), giving nested tessellations: thick walls between countries, thin between provinces, jagged parent borders, lineage values, N levels.
master.look:
A political map: large irregular countries with thick borders subdivided into provinces with thin borders, borders of the big regions made of small-cell polygon edges (jagged, not Voronoi-straight). As a crack field: dry mud with primary cracks and secondary cracks inside each plate; giraffe / tortoise-shell patterns. With 3-4 levels it is a fractal Voronoi where every level nests inside the previous.
[Provinces, cell-relations] Political map or geological map: jagged, polygon-stepped borders at 2-3 scales, blocks of related cell values, thin internal cell lines optional. Also patchy farmland, plate tectonics masks, biome IDs with shared borders. Prototyped: rel_province, window 32 wide.
master.algorithm:
Level 0: the normal fine Cellular window (scale 1). Level l has scale k^l (k = Ratio, e.g. 3) with its own jittered lattice.
Parent lookup for a point P at level l -> level l+1: cells q in floor(P/k^{l+1} - 0.5) + {0,1}^D (the 2^D coarse cells whose centres are nearest to P); parent = argmin |P - Q_q| over those 2^D coarse points; returns (position, hash). Because it depends only on P, every sample computes the same parent for the same fine point: window-consistent by construction. (It is 'approximately Voronoi': true coarse Voronoi would need the 3^D block; offer Exact flag.)
For each of the 3^D fine window points compute the chain of ancestors up to Levels (fixed loop), storing hashes.
Outputs:
  LineageValue: sum_l Amp^l * rnd11(hash_l(F1)) -> clustered colours (provinces vary around their country's value)
  AncestorValue(L): rnd11(hash_L(F1)) -> coarse regions whose borders follow fine cell walls (jagged polygon coastlines)
  AncestorLookup: Source sampled at the level-L ancestor position of F1 (CellularLookup with jagged borders)
  Walls: divergence level div(F1,j) = first level where ancestors of F1 and j differ (0 if different parents at level 1, up to Levels); mult(div) from a per-level Width table; W = min_{j != F1} (d_j - d_1) * mult(div(F1,j))  (or exact wall distance from CellularFracture). Continuous by the min argument: the term for the cell across any wall is 0 on both sides.
3D/4D: identical with 2^D = 8/16 coarse candidates per fine point.

[Provinces, cell-relations] For each window cell c: P1(c)=floor((c+hop)/B1) with hop=round(Hop*rnd(h_c)) per axis (plus an optional low-frequency sin wobble of c), P2(c)=P1(c)>>log2(B2). Pass 1: F1 owner o. Pass 2: for j != o: rank = 2 if P2 differs, 1 if P1 differs, else 0; wd=(d_j^2-d_o^2)/2 (constant denominator); line=max(line, depth[rank]*profile(wd/width[rank])); coast=min(coast, wd where rank>=1). Outputs: border lines with thickness by rank, cluster value (v2*a+v1*b+v0*c from hashes of P2, P1, own), value with borders, distance to the nearest province border (coast).
master.why_new: CellularValue/Lookup produce one scale; stacking two Cellular nodes gives independent, non-nested partitions (fine walls cross coarse walls). Nesting (fine cells never straddle a coarse border) is what a graph cannot express.
master.simd_plan: Lattice-only parent arithmetic: integer add, arithmetic shift, integer compare on two id components per axis, masks for the rank. 3^D window for pass 1 and 2. Estimate 1.5-2x CellularDistance. No source evaluation. Power-of-two block sizes keep Floor as a shift. The window should be safe at 3^D as in PolyGauge, but the proto used 5x5.
master.continuity: Border line output is C0 thanks to the constant denominator, including across merged walls (d_i=d_j on the merged wall, so wd matches on both sides). Not formally run through check. Value outputs are discontinuous by design.
master.params: Levels (int 1..4), Ratio (float, coarse/fine), Level Widths (per-level wall multiplier table or Width + Width Gain), Amp Gain (lineage), Output enum {LineageValue, AncestorValue, AncestorLookup, Walls}, Exact Parent (bool, 3^D search), Grid Jitter per level, Source, Feature Scale.
master.risks:
3D cost grows fast with levels; 2^D parent search makes parent regions slightly non-Voronoi (fine in practice). With Ratio < 2 the nesting is barely visible. Walls between different-parent cells are thicker but not longer-range; a 'thick border' is still only one fine cell wide at most (Width <= margin).
[Provinces, cell-relations] Small hop leaves the square block visible at large scale; large hop gives detached exclaves (sometimes desirable). Coast distance saturates at window reach (about 1 fine cell), so it is a shoreline band, not a global distance.
master.variant_notes: Opposite direction to NestedVoronoi: fine cells inherit a coarse id so coarse borders are made of fine walls. Parent lookup options: nearest coarse point in a 2^D block, or integer block with hashed hop (cheaper, Provinces).
